companyDescription: Pre-revenue micro-reactor developer (ZEUS, ODIN) · KRONOS MMR construction permit application now formally DOCKETED by the NRC for a University of Illinois site (concrete 2027 review / mid-2027 construction timeline) · New nuclear-powered AI infrastructure LOI with IP3 · $580M cash
priceNote: Live $11.87 (-2.4%) at Oct 26, 2026 open — down ~26% from $16 at the Sep 29 report, at its 52-week low ($11.79-$49.50). Market cap ~$637M on 53.7M shares. Since the Sep 29 reports, this board's small caps fell 21-41% after the Sep 16 hike and the hot Sep CPI (Oct 14). This is a sector/size selloff that SPY-based regime notes don't capture, so drawdowns here say as much about the tape as the thesis.
summary: REFRESH (prior report Sep 29, 2026): KRONOS is under NRC construction-permit review with the University of Illinois. NNE has since signed IMPSA for critical KRONOS components (construction targeted H2 2027) and bought NRC-licensed fuel-processing assets from Radnostix, yet the stock fell ~26% to its 52-week low as SMR names de-rated. The selloff lifts consensus upside to ~213% ($37.14), so the Moon case now clears the 200% bar (it didn't at $16). regulatory_approval is a Tier-2 LEADER (+5.3pp vs +2.0pp, n=8). There is no survival flag (large cash balance). The weakness is that the binary (permit) is multi-year, so near-term moves are sentiment-driven. Base trimmed from +55% to +45% (above the lane's realized 30d P90 of +25.9%; written-Base bias +72.7pp). It assumes 6-12 months of NRC review milestones. แนะนำ 2-3% ของ portfolio เท่านั้น — ถ้า thesis fail ลงได้ 30-50%.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 results
catalysts.description: First update since the IMPSA master services agreement (KRONOS component engineering and fabrication) and the Radnostix fuel-processing asset acquisition. The read is NRC review progress and cash deployment. Exact date not yet announced.

catalysts.name: KRONOS MMR construction permit — NRC review
catalysts.description: Application docketed for the University of Illinois site, with the University supporting technical review. Construction targeted for H2 2027; IMPSA signed for critical components.

catalysts.name: Nuclear-powered AI infrastructure LOI (IP3)
catalysts.description: Non-binding LOI with IP3 Corporation for nuclear-powered AI data infrastructure.

risks: Pre-revenue (TTM revenue ~$0.2M). The KRONOS permit review and H2 2027 construction start make this a multi-year thesis with no near-term binary.
SMR/advanced-nuclear sentiment is volatile: the stock is -67% from its $49.50 high despite steady regulatory progress.
The IP3 AI-infrastructure tie-up is still a non-binding LOI.
Acquisitions (Radnostix fuel processing) and IMPSA fabrication commitments increase spending ahead of any revenue.
DOE and policy preferences have at times favored large reactors over micro-reactors, a sector-level headwind.

estimateDates.note: NRC review status, IMPSA/Radnostix integration, cash

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds at 3.75-4.00% after the surprise Sep 16, 2026 hike (first since 2023). The Oct 27-28 FOMC is priced ~93% hold / ~7% +25bp as of Oct 25 — but hike odds briefly spiked to ~44% after the hot Sep CPI print on Oct 14, so the path stays two-sided.
macroRisk.inflationNote: September CPI +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y headline; core +0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y — both above consensus. Headline re-acceleration keeps a further 2026 hike live.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Pre-revenue but well-capitalized advanced-nuclear developer. Rates move the long-duration multiple (cash flows are 2028+) more than solvency.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — Oct 28 hold is priced (~93%), but hot CPI keeps a further 2026 hike live. Small, cash-burning names have already absorbed most of this tape's damage, so a hold is mildly supportive and a surprise hike is the main macro tail.

catalystSpot.preRunup: No run-up: NNE is ~26% below the Sep 29 report and at its 52-week low (-67% from the $49.50 high), despite the IMPSA and Radnostix announcements. SMR names have de-rated as a group.

postWin.note: SMR-sector names have shown 5-25% pops on positive DOE/NRC regulatory milestones. Per this run's tier2 feedback, regulatory_approval is a lane-wide LEADER catalystType (+5.3pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=8), supporting normal conviction/sizing here.

postLose.note: NNE's own decline from its 52-week high ($60.87) to current levels ($16.00) — a ~74% drawdown — remains the most direct same-company precedent for how far SMR-sector sentiment can turn against these names on DOE policy news unrelated to company-specific execution.

spotSizing.reason: 2.5%. regulatory_approval is a Tier-2 LEADER (+5.3pp vs +2.0pp, n=8; 2/8 windows had SPY down >2%), and a large cash balance removes survival risk. The NRC timeline is multi-year with no near-term binary, and the lane scoreboard is weak (hitRate 4.9%, n=41).

stopPreCatalyst.note: Wider than the regulatory_approval medianMAE (-25.0%, n=8). A further break well below the 52-week low signals a sector-wide capitulation, not a company-specific failure.

stopPostCatalyst.note: If the NRC review stalls (e.g., requests for additional information that push construction past 2027), exit.
